INDEPENDENT REVIEW 4 OF 1.24.40'S PDF TOOLS -- 2026-11-26
Build under review: lantern_1240_r4.html (version 1.24.40, frozen copy, sha256 7ce86d325a43bf93...), served as index.html
in Playwright's Chromium. "Old" is 1.24.39 (old_1239_index.html, sha256 79891e0b1e916e0f...). I did not see this code
being written and changed nothing outside this folder. Line numbers below are of the frozen file.

RESULT: 831 checks, 79 failed (cases.json; `python3 run_review.py <new.html> <old.html>` from this folder).
  hyph 439 / 35 failed   ls 48 / 6   fold 151 / 10   std14 14 / 11   deep 41 / 8   links 31 / 2   forms 26 / 7   sweep 81 / 0

HOW IT WAS TRIED
PDFs (make_fixtures.py; all made by programs that are not Lantern):
  reportlab  h_rl (4 pages: one column; two aligned columns drawn word by word, justified so word gaps reach 130 pt
             against a 26 pt column gap; the same two columns drawn a line at a time with Tw, the right column 6.5 pt
             lower; three columns 16 pt apart, the third 4 pt lower; labels turned 90 and -90; a table). Breaks with
             '-', U+2010, U+2011 and a drawn U+00AD; traps: "Range set to 10 -" / "20 V", "Signed: Smith -" / "Jones",
             a short paragraph-ending "Next step: pre-", next-column words at the same height (Carlton, Dunmore).
             ls_rl (letters one at a time at 0.3/0.6 em; digit cells at 12/14/18 pt pitch; keys A B C D at 14 pt; a
             comb box; a grid X O X O X). fold_rl (DejaVu Sans, code points exactly as typed: Turkish I/i, Greek with
             tonos/dialytika/final sigma, U+FB00-FB06, e + U+0301). forms_rl (AcroForm on two pages, appearances by
             reportlab) and forms_noap (the owner field's appearance removed, /NeedAppearances).
  pikepdf    std14 (Helvetica, Times-Roman, Courier, Helvetica-Bold, Times-Italic, Helvetica-Oblique with no /Widths,
             fi fl ff ffi ffl by /Differences; Times-Roman and Courier with no /Encoding, fi fl as \256 \257);
             deep (forms nested 70 deep, a word at depths 1 2 10 32 48 63 64 65 66 70; a form that draws itself; two
             forms that draw each other); links (URI links holding "Ormskirk" plain, %4F, %72, upper case, on marked and
             unmarked pages; a /Names /Dests tree and a catalog /Dests holding it; links and bookmarks going to them;
             bookmark titles holding it, one UTF-16); forms_acro2 (review 3's Acrobat-style f_acro after a cover page).
  pdflatex   h_tex (twocolumn, then multicol three columns; justified; TeX's own hyphenation and explicit breaks);
             ls_tex (kerned capitals, microtype \textls, inline equations, single-character tabular cells).
  xelatex    ls_xe (U <= 230 V, I >= 2 A, f = 50 Hz +- 1 %, equations, tabular); fold_xe (DejaVu Serif, as fold_rl).
  LibreOffice h_lo (two- and three-column justified sections, soft hyphens); ls_lo (plain single letters; Writer's
             own letter-spacing).
  Chromium   h_chrome (CSS columns 2 and 3, justify, &shy;, names with their own hyphen, a list with " -", a table
             with cells ending "-", labels turned 90 and -90); ls_chrome (letter-spacing 0.05 to 1 em with "(0.2em)"
             signs; single-character cells, inline-block keys, a comb, equations, plain lines of single letters).
Oracles: poppler (pdftotext -bbox, -bbox-layout, -layout, pdftoppm), pdfplumber/pdfminer (letter boxes, AFM widths),
pypdf (text, fields, outline), pikepdf (annotations, destinations), qpdf (--check, --qdf), tesseract, reportlab's Adobe
metrics, and each fixture's own design (what was drawn where). The runner imports review 3's r3lib.py and pdfhand.py
from ../pdf_review3_1240 (not changed); its outputs go to the scratchpad's r4out folder.

FINDINGS
1. [L] A word broken at a line's end in justified columns drawn word by word, and in TeX's multicol, is not found, so
   Redact leaves both halves.
   Smallest: h_rl.pdf page 2, search "Hollingsworth": 0 places (expected 1: "Hollings-" ends the right column's line at
   x 513, "worth" starts the next line at x 316). The same on that page for "Quarm-"/"by"; page 4 (three columns):
   "Ashworth-"/"Bramley" (column 1) and "Pember-"/"ton" (column 2); h_tex.pdf page 2 (multicol): "elec-"/"trohydraulic"
   (column 2), "recon-"/"firmed" and "Winterbottom-"/"Smythe" (column 3). Lines drawn a run at a time (page 3, Tw) and
   TeX's twocolumn page are found.
   Evidence: redacting ["Ashworth-Bramley", "Hollingsworth", "Pemberton", ...] leaves "Hollingsworth" (page 2),
   "AshworthBramley" and "Pemberton," (page 4) in poppler's text of the copy; evidence/1_*.png and 2_*.png show them
   unboxed.
   Traced (marksOf, lines 53135-53200): an "edge" is a cluster of >= max(3, 0.2 x lines) run starts that follow a gap of
   over 0.8 of the size. In justified text every word follows such a gap, so three word starts that happen to line up
   make a false edge; the word's column is taken as the one nearest edge at or left of it, and when no line under it
   starts there the fallback is "where this run's piece of line starts" -- which in word-by-word justified text is the
   hyphenated word itself. Direction: try every edge at or left of the word, nearest first, until one has a line under
   it starting there (and the word joined); ask more of an edge than 3 starts on a page of 15 lines, or count only starts
   that follow a gap at least as wide as the widest gap seen between columns; let the fallback walk back over word gaps.

2. [L] A word broken at the foot of a column and finished at the head of the next column is not found.
   Smallest: h_chrome.pdf, three CSS columns: "Winter-" (U+00AD + U+2010) ends column 2 at (353, 389), "bourne" starts
   column 3 at (392, 510); search "Winterbourne" finds 8 of the page's 9. TeX, Writer and browsers all break words there.
   Direction: when no line under the word within 2.5 sizes starts at the column's edge, try the first line of the next
   column to the right (the top-most line with a run starting at the next edge).

3. [O] A dash standing alone at a line's end is taken for a hyphen.
   Smallest: h_rl.pdf page 1, "Range set to 10 -" / "20 V on the panel meter.": search "1020" marks "10 -" and "20";
   "Signed: Smith -" / "Jones witnessed..." is found as "SmithJones". The same in Chromium's list (h_chrome).
   Traced: the line-end pattern /(\S+?)\s?[-‐‑­]$/ (line 53172) allows a space before the hyphen.
   Direction: no space between the letters and the hyphen, and the piece before it ends in a letter.

4. [O] A short line that ends a paragraph in a hyphen is joined to the next paragraph's first word.
   Smallest: h_rl.pdf pages 1-3: "Next step: pre-" (a 70 pt line in a 240 pt column) / "Start checks on both pumps
   today.": search "prestart" finds it. Direction: only a line that reaches near its column's right side can end in a
   break (no typesetter hyphenates a paragraph's short last line).

5. [O] Table cells are paired with the next row's first cell.
   Smallest: h_chrome.pdf: a table row "Valve | AX- | Kirkby-" over "Seal | Lonsdale | spare": "AXSeal" and "KirkbySeal"
   are found ("AX-" is in the middle of its row). Direction: join a run only to a run under the start of its own piece
   of line (or at an edge its own piece starts at), never to an edge left of other text on its line.
   (Not counted: in h_rl's reportlab table, "BX-" is joined to "Hawes" in the cell under it, the same table column; a
   cell wrapped onto two lines looks just like that.)

6. [R][O] Single letters separated by ordinary spaces are read as one word, with the label before them, in a browser's
   PDF; and a row of single-letter keys is joined.
   Smallest: ls_chrome.pdf, the HTML "<p>Grades: A B C D E</p>" (no CSS): Text reading gives "Grades:ABCDE";
   "Keys: <span>A</span><span>B</span>..." (inline-block, 16 pt wide) gives "Keys:ABCD"; ls_rl.pdf, letters drawn one at
   a time at a 14 pt pitch: "Keys: ABCD". 1.24.39 and poppler: "Grades: A B C D E", "Keys: A B C D".
   Not joined (all pass): "Answer: A B C or D", "Choose one of A B C D E and F.", "Rows a b c d e f in the grid.",
   "Sizes: S M L XL", "Initials J R R T Tolkien", table cells a..h, inline-block Q W E R T Y, digit cells at 12/14/18 pt,
   the comb, "X O X O X", equations in Chromium, pdfTeX and xelatex, "U <= 230 V, I >= 2 A", pdfTeX's kerned words.
   Traced (line 49342): Chromium draws no space glyphs, and letters one space apart have gaps all equal to the space's
   advance: an even gap, which is what the rule looks for; the "lone signs" pass then reaches further. Direction: a gap
   within ~0.05 em of the font's space advance is a word space, not letter-spacing (a browser's letter-spacing makes a
   word gap = space + spacing, wider than the letter gap); never take away the space after a piece of several letters.

7. [D] Letter-spacing of exactly 1 em is not read as words.
   Smallest: ls_chrome.pdf "SOWERBY (1em)" -> "S O W E R B Y ( 1 e m )" (1.24.39 the same). The test gmin < ln.size
   (line 49358) is strict, and at 1 em the gap equals the size. Direction: allow up to ~1.05 of the size.

8. [D] Standard fonts with no /Widths: ligatures measured as their letters, not by Adobe's metrics.
   Smallest: std14.pdf. fi in Times-Roman is given f + i (611/1000) instead of Adobe's 556, in Courier 1200 instead of
   600; ff, ffi and ffl are given their letters' widths instead of none. Words after them sit up to 36 pt right of where
   poppler and pdfplumber (pdfminer's AFM tables) put them, which agree to 0.1 pt (Courier "office" right edge +36.0;
   Helvetica "after" +25.3). Lantern draws the page with its own widths (evidence/3_*.png: poppler above, Lantern
   below), and its marks follow its drawing, so a copy covers what Lantern drew; but the claim ("as poppler and pdf.js")
   does not hold, and Lantern's page differs from every other viewer's. Direction: look up the glyph name in the AFM
   widths (fi, fl) and give a name the AFM lacks (ff, ffi, ffl) width 0 (or /MissingWidth).

9. [L] (also in 1.24.39) A standard font with no /Encoding is read as WinAnsi, not as its built-in StandardEncoding.
   Smallest: std14.pdf, Times-Roman and Courier with no /Encoding: \256 \257 are read "(R)" and macron instead of fi, fl:
   "Pro(R)le (macron)ow", so search for "Profile" or "finance" finds nothing there and Redact leaves it. poppler reads
   fi, fl. (StandardEncoding also differs from WinAnsi at 0x27, 0x60 and most codes above 0x7F.) Direction: a
   non-symbolic standard font with no /Encoding uses StandardEncoding (Symbol and ZapfDingbats their own).

10. [D] In a redacted copy, pypdf reads the kept words split.
   Smallest: fold_xe.pdf (xelatex) redacted for "Ormskirk": poppler reads every kept word whole with its accents right,
   but pypdf reads "ISTAN BUL" (dotted I), "Fer nandez" (accent kept on the a), "A ngstr om" (ring and diaeresis kept),
   "Pi AP ADOP OYLOS", "fi nance", "fl uent"; fold_rl: "Izm ir". The copy writes every letter as its own Tj with its own Tz
   and Tm (qpdf --qdf of the copy, e.g. "108.24588 Tz 1 0 0 1 88.50368 725.344 Tm (A) Tj"); pypdf (6.17.0) evidently does
   not take Tz into a letter's advance, sees gaps and puts spaces. The claim names pypdf. Direction: write each word as
   one TJ with numeric adjustments instead of a Tz per letter.

11. [D] U+017F (long s) is not folded: xelatex writes U+FB05 as "long s, t" in its ToUnicode, and "stop" does not find
   it (fold_xe). U+FB05 itself is found (fold_rl). Direction: fold U+017F to s, as NFKC does.

12. [D] Redact with words drops the links that go to a destination it renames.
   Smallest: links.pdf, redact "Ormskirk" (page 1 marked): the destinations "Ormskirk-plan" (/Names) and /sec.Ormskirk
   (catalog /Dests) are renamed LtnD1 and LtnD2, and the bookmarks to them still go to pages 2 and 3, but page 3's two
   links to them are gone. Traced (line 52945): on a page not marked, a link is dropped when holds() finds the word in
   its /Dest or /A /D, before scrub() renames the destination. Direction: leave /Dest and GoTo /D out of holds() (they
   are renamed), or rename first and test after.

13. [D] Redact makes every form field of every page part of its page as soon as one marked page has a field.
   Smallest: forms_rl.pdf (reportlab, fields on pages 1 and 2): redact "Ormskirk" (page 1 only): page 2's "city" and
   "agreed" are made part of the page and /AcroForm is removed (evidence/4_*.png); marking only page 2 does the same to
   page 1's three fields. forms_noap likewise. Where no marked page has a field (forms_acro2) the form stays whole (pass).
   Traced (needsFlat/flatFirst, lines 52828-52841): forms is true when a marked page has a field, and P.flatten is
   called with {forms: true}, which flattens all pages' fields (its pages option is for comments). Direction: flatten
   the marked pages' fields only, and keep /AcroForm with /Fields pruned to the fields left.

14. [D] (preview only) The mark Redact's search shows for a field value with its own appearance is placed by Lantern's
   own padding, not where the appearance draws it: forms_rl "Ormskirk" marked 121.3-169.5, drawn 124.0-172.0 (poppler on
   qpdf's flattening); the shown mark leaves the last 2.5 pt of the "k". The copy is right: after flattening the word is
   found again where it is drawn, and every inked pixel of the word is black in the copy (forms_rl and forms_noap).
   Direction: take the value's position from the appearance stream when there is one.

15. [D] (beyond the claimed limit) Forms nested deeper than 64 are neither read nor drawn, and a redacted copy loses
   them: deep.pdf, words at depths 65, 66 and 70 are missing from Text reading, from the copy's text and from its picture
   (tesseract); poppler reads and draws all 70. Depth 64 and the loops are fine. Low: qpdf's stamps wrap one level each.
   Direction: loops are already stopped by the forms in progress, so the cap could be far higher (poppler's is over 70).

WHICH FAILED CHECKS ARE NOT FINDINGS
  - ls_tex "WAREHOUSE NORTH ..." (microtype \textls: "WAREHO U S E N O RT H"; 1.24.39 "WA R E H O U S E ...") and ls_lo
    (Writer's fo:letter-spacing: letters one by one, as 1.24.39 and poppler): letter-spacing not made by a browser,
    beyond what the rule names. Reported for information.
  - deep: the eight rows at depths over 64 are beyond the claim (finding 15).
  - std14 "every poppler word has a Lantern word to match" and the two "covered by its mark (vs poppler's box)" rows are
    consequences of findings 8 and 9 (Lantern's place differs from poppler's; its own copy covers its own drawing).
  Oracle and fixture faults found while building the run, and mended before the final run (none remains in cases.json):
  r3lib's HERE shadowed the runner's (it looked in the wrong folder); "by" is on a page many times and the oracle took the
  first; Chromium writes U+00AD inside unbroken words and poppler passes it on (the oracle now drops it); poppler joins
  Writer's narrow three columns into one line and saw no breaks there (h_lo and h_chrome counts are now the design: each
  paragraph holds each name once, 7 and 9; stray marks judged only where the oracle found every place); xelatex composes
  e + U+0301 (only fold_rl tries a separate accent); the TeX source had "\parCheck" and a thin space before "V"; the
  sweep against poppler skips this review's letter-spaced PDFs (poppler reads spaced letters one by one).

WHAT PASSED
  Rule 1: one column (all four hyphens; "Ashworth-Bramley" found with and without its hyphen, both halves marked, no
  stray marks); two columns drawn a run at a time with Tw, the right column 6.5 pt lower (every break in both columns);
  the cross-column traps ("AshworthCarlton", "AshworthDunmore", "HollingsBramley" never found); turned labels at 90 and
  -90 in reportlab and Chromium ("Quenby-"/"Ashton", "Ravens-"/"worth"); TeX twocolumn page 1 (all breaks, incl.
  "Featherstone-"/"haugh", "Dun-"/"more", "rep-"/"resentatives", "de-"/"pot"); Writer's three columns (7 of 7 for every
  name); Chromium two and three columns except finding 2; names with U+00AD inside unbroken words (Chromium) found.
  Rule 2: Chromium 0.05-0.75 em with the "(0.2em)" signs read with the words, reportlab 0.3 and 0.6 em, and every trap
  listed under finding 6 left apart.
  Rule 3: every search on fold_rl and fold_xe (Turkish four ways, Greek both cases with tonos/dialytika/final sigma,
  U+FB00-FB06, e + U+0301 found by the typed word with the accented letter covered to its right edge); poppler reads
  every kept word of the redacted copies with its accents on the right letters; the Greek name and Rene gone from
  poppler's text and from the bytes.
  Rule 5: the self-drawing form and the ring read once, drawn, redacted in seconds; depth 1-64 read, kept and drawn.
  Rule 6: URI links holding the word (plain, %4F, %72, upper case) dropped on marked and unmarked pages; other links on
  unmarked pages kept; both kinds of named destination renamed and still naming the same pages; every bookmark goes to
  its page; titles holding the word get three block letters, the rest kept (UTF-16 too); qpdf --check clean; the word
  nowhere in the copy's bytes (latin-1, UTF-16, shown strings, %-encoded).
  Rule 7: field values found by search; the no-appearance value's mark is Helvetica's width (48.0 pt) inside the field;
  marked pages' widgets gone and values out of the bytes, other words still searchable; forms_acro2's form kept whole.
  Sweep: 81 page readings (60 earlier fixtures sampled at random, seed 4, and this review's PDFs other than ls_*): none
  worse than 1.24.39 against poppler; three better (e_drawing, r_invoice_lin pages 1 and 2).

NOT CHECKED
  pdf.js and Acrobat (not here): the std14 widths were judged by poppler and pdfminer. 1.24.39 has no redactMarks or
  redact API, so rules 1, 3, 6 and 7 have no comparison with it (finding 6 is a regression in Text reading, which both
  have). The tile itself was not driven (the API only). Word-by-word justified columns came from reportlab, not from
  Word or InDesign. Writer here has no hyphenation dictionaries, so its breaks are at soft hyphens only.
